Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet()` tries to check that `isUnixSymlink()` returns false for a Zip entry that has multiple Unix permission flags set. It fails according to the report because the method currently returns true incorrectly for entries with Unix permissions 177777.

Inspecting the code of `isUnixSymlink()` reveals that it returns true if the Unix mode bits of the entry, masked with `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`, equal `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. Unix mode is retrieved from external attributes if the platform is Unix.

`UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` is defined as octal 0120000, which corresponds to the Unix symbolic link file type bits.

The bug stems from `isUnixSymlink()` only checking these bits for a precise match, i.e., it returns true if at least these bits are set, disregarding if any other bits beyond the symbolic link bits are also set. Thus, if multiple flags are combined, like 177777 (octal), the check still returns true, which is incorrect.

The failing test confirms that `isUnixSymlink()` should return false if more than one bit flag in the Unix mode is set, not just if the symbolic link bits are contained.

Therefore, the root cause is that `isUnixSymlink()` implementation does not ensure exclusively that the Unix mode bits equal the link flag bits exactly; it only checks if the link bits are set among potentially other bits.

No relevant clues were found in recent bug reports; the primary evidence comes from the current bug report, failing test, and code examination.

The fix should require `isUnixSymlink()` to verify that the Unix mode represents exactly a symbolic link type, not just that it contains the link flag bits, i.e., `(getUnixMode() & FILE_TYPE_MASK) == LINK_FLAG` where `FILE_TYPE_MASK` masks out all file type bits. This mask seems missing now.

Hence, the diagnosis is that `isUnixSymlink()` returns true if any bits overlap with `LINK_FLAG` whereas it should only return true if the Unix mode matches exactly the symbolic link file type bits alone, excluding other flags or bits.

This explains the failure and guides the fix location.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
